subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Johnson <ava.johnson@kitebank.com>
Cc: dylan@redwood.ai, marissa@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan

Hi Ava — thanks again for taking the demo today. Really appreciated the thoughtful questions from your team. As promised, here’s a short recap and a proposed POC plan to evaluate Redwood across the main success criteria we discussed.

Quick recap of the demo
- Showed low-latency chat and batch embeddings flow for your customer support use case
- Demonstrated prefix caching and cost/latency dashboard for model routing
- Highlighted Dedicated capacity option for predictable throughput

Proposed POC (outline) — goals and success criteria
1) Success criteria (target metrics)
   - Latency: 95th percentile rolling < 400ms on 1k qps emulated load for chat endpoints
   - Cost: per-endpoint token cost <= target threshold we discussed ($0.0009/token equivalent)
   - Quality: intent-classification accuracy maintained within 2% of baseline on your eval set (provided)
   - Stability: 99.9% availability for the routed endpoints over the 2-week run

2) Technical scope
   - Data: we’ll use a 3k-example eval set you provide (anonymized), plus a live proxy to production traffic (read-only) for 48 hours of live sampling
   - Integrations: short-lived API key + IP allowlist; optional SSO for console access

3) Timeline
   - Week 0 (kickoff): alignment call, access & roles, finalize eval set
   - Week 1: test environment + ingest eval set; smoke tests
   - Week 2: run load/quality experiments; collect metrics and logs
   - End of Week 2: final review and recommendation

4) Ownership
   - Redwood: Camila Reyes (AM) + Dylan Brooks (Solutions Eng) — onboarding, infra, and results analysis
   - KiteBank: Ava Johnson (Product) + your platform lead (TBD) — provide eval set, grant access, and validate results

5) Next steps (requested from you)
   - Confirm the eval set owner and share a sample (3–5 examples) by EOD Friday
   - Confirm an initial kickoff window next week (I’m proposing Mon 3/27 or Tue 3/28 morning PST)

I’ve attached a short POC plan and a checklist with required items for your platform team. Happy to iterate — goal is to make this low-friction and measurable.

Attachments: KiteBank-POC-Plan-v1.pdf (application/pdf), Redwood-POC-Checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai
From: Ava Johnson <ava.johnson@kitebank.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform@kitebank.com
Date: 2028-03-22T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan

Thanks Camila — great demo. Quick notes from our side after internal sync: 

- The success criteria look good overall. One ask: can we relax the latency target to 95p < 450ms given our current network egress characteristics? Not a blocker — just want to set realistic expectations.
- For quality, we’ll use the standard intent/slot eval set (we’ll share the canonical train/dev/eval split). Accuracy within 2% is reasonable.
- We will need a short security checklist before we grant test access — SOC 2 attestation and data handling notes. Our platform team (cc’ed) will follow up with specifics.

A couple items we’ll own:
- I’ll send a sample of the eval set (5 examples) by Friday.
- Platform will confirm a best point-of-contact for access (likely Miguel from infra).

Kickoff: Mon 3/27 morning PST works for us. Can you do 9:30am?

Thanks,
Ava
Ava Johnson
Product Manager, Conversational AI | KiteBank
ava.johnson@kitebank.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Johnson <ava.johnson@kitebank.com>
Cc: dylan@redwood.ai, marissa@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-23T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan

Hi Ava — thanks for the quick response and for looping in platform. 9:30am PST on Mon 3/27 is perfect; I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Responses to your notes:
- Latency target: we can set the target to 95p < 450ms for the POC run, and run an optimization pass with Dylan during the experiment window to see if we can hit 400ms without increasing cost materially.
- Security docs: attaching a short SOC2 summary and our data handling notes for the POC (see attachment). If platform needs additional artifacts, Dylan can join the security call.

Practical next steps (from Redwood):
- I’ll open a short-lived API key and create an allowlist. Please provide the CIDR/IP or the contact who will request access.
- Share the 5-sample eval set by EOD Friday so we can sanity-check ingestion.
- On Mon: 30min kickoff to confirm access, test data flow, and success metric dashboards.

Updated attachments: KiteBank-POC-Plan-v1.pdf (updated with latency note), SOC2-snapshot.pdf, Redwood-POC-Checklist.xlsx

Looking forward — I’ve put Dylan on the kickoff and he’ll lead the runbook creation.

Best,
Camila
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai
From: Ava Johnson <ava.johnson@kitebank.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform@kitebank.com
Date: 2028-03-23T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan

Perfect — confirmed. 9:30am PST Mon 3/27 is on the calendar (invite received). Miguel from platform will own access; he’s cc’d now (platform@kitebank.com) and will send IPs and the eval sample by EOD Friday.

We approve the adjusted latency target (95p < 450ms) for the POC. Please proceed with opening the API key and the allowlist. Looking forward to the run.

Thanks,
Ava
